message.content:
It depends a bit on what you mean by “interface.”  
Here are a few common interpretations and how you’d get detailed information for each:

| Context | Typical command / method | What you’ll see |
|---------|--------------------------|-----------------|
| **Network interface on a Linux/Unix host** | `ip addr show <iface>` or `ifconfig <iface> -a` | IP addresses, MAC, MTU, state, flags, etc. |
| **Network interface on Windows** | `Get-NetAdapter -Name "<iface>"` (PowerShell) or `ipconfig /all` | Same as above plus DHCP lease, DNS suffix, etc. |
| **Network interface on macOS** | `ifconfig <iface>` or `networksetup -getinfo <iface>` | IP, MAC, MTU, state, etc. |
| **API endpoint (REST)** | `curl -v https://api.example.com/<resource>` | HTTP headers, status code, JSON payload, rate‑limit headers, etc. |
| **Programming interface (e.g., Java class, Python module)** | Use introspection (`dir()`, `help()`, `pydoc`) or IDE’s “Go to definition” | Method signatures, docstrings, attributes, etc. |
| **Device connector interface (hardware)** | Use vendor‑specific tools (e.g., `ethtool`, `lspci`, `lshw`) | Driver version, link speed, duplex, supported features, etc. |

If you let me know which type of interface you’re interested in (network, API, programming, hardware, etc.) I can give you a more precise set of commands or code snippets.
